items.prose: A backtest has 2,016 trading days. The scoring model's training cut-off falls after day 1,638.
items.question: What share of the backtest is in the clean window? Give 4 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Count the days after the cut-off.

byKey.before: That is the share before the cut-off.

explain.text: $2016 - 1638 = 378$ clean days, a share of 0.1875: under a fifth of the backtest tests reading.

items.prose: In a clean window, a text signal's daily P&L has mean 0.08% and standard deviation 1.2%.
items.question: What is its annualised Sharpe ratio? Give 2 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Annualise the daily ratio by $\sqrt{252}$.

byKey.x252: You multiplied by 252, not its square root.

explain.text: The daily ratio is 0.0667; times 15.875 that is 1.06.

items.prose: A model given a 20-word filing's opening writes back its first 15 words exactly.
items.question: What share of the filing's 5-grams does it reproduce? Give 4 decimal places.

feedback.correct: 16 five-grams in all, 11 inside the shared 15 words: 0.6875.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Count 5-grams lying inside the shared words.

byKey.words: 0.75 is the share of words; count runs of five.

explain.text: $20 - 5 + 1 = 16$ five-grams, of which $15 - 5 + 1 = 11$ are reproduced: 0.6875, strong evidence the model has read the filing.

items.prose: A desk sets positions at the 16:00 close. A broker note arrives on Thursday at 16:05.
items.question: Which decision should it feed?

options.why: Thursday's positions were set at 16:00, before the note existed.
This desk trades only at the close.

feedback.correct: Friday's close, the first decision after it.
feedback.generic: Not quite. When is the next decision after 16:05 on Thursday?

explain.text: A document feeds the first decision at or after its publication time.

items.prose: A decayed text feature uses a half-life of 3 days.
items.question: What weight does a note 1.5 days old get? Give 4 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Raise 0.5 to age over half-life.

byKey.half: 0.5 is the weight at one full half-life, 3 days.
byKey.linear: Decay is exponential, not a straight line.

explain.text: Half a half-life leaves $\sqrt{0.5} = 0.7071$ of the weight.

items.prose: Annual results for the year ending 31 December are published on 14 February. A dataset stamps them 31 December.
items.question: How many calendar days of look-ahead does the stamp create?

feedback.correct: 31 days of January plus 14 of February: 45.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Count from 31 December to 14 February.

explain.text: From 31 December to 14 February is 45 days, six weeks of trading on numbers nobody had.

items.prose: A masking test on 36 headlines gives a mean score change of 0.06, raw minus masked, with standard deviation 0.24.
items.question: What is the standard error of the mean change? Give 2 decimal places.

feedback.correct: $0.24/\sqrt{36} = 0.04$; the change is 1.5 standard errors from 0, not yet convincing.

byKey.sd: That is the spread of single changes.
byKey.over-n: You divided by 36; divide by its square root, 6.

explain.text: $0.24/6 = 0.04$, so a mean of 0.06 is 1.5 standard errors: mask more headlines before deciding.

items.prose: A fold trains on 4 notes. 'refinancing' appears in 1 of them; across all 10 notes of every year it appears in 6.
items.question: What IDF should the fold give 'refinancing'? Give 4 decimal places.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Use only the training notes.

byKey.all: That uses all 10 notes, test years included.

explain.text: Within the fold, $n = 4$ and df $= 1$: $\ln\frac{5}{2} + 1 = 1.9163$. The all-years figure would carry test-year frequencies back.

items.prose: A team tried 30 prompt and model combinations over 3 clean years and reports the best Sharpe ratio, 1.8.
items.question: What is the haircut Sharpe ratio? Give 2 decimal places.

byKey.noise: That is the noise best; subtract it from 1.8.

explain.text: Thirty tries over three years give noise a best near 1.51, so 1.8 is worth about 0.29.

items.prose: A researcher z-scores a text feature with the mean and standard deviation of the whole backtest, then runs walk-forward folds on it.
items.question: What is wrong?

options.text: The scaling used future data; fit it inside each fold
Nothing: z-scoring is not a model
options.why: Any statistic computed from the future is look-ahead, scaling included.

options.text: Only the standard deviation leaks, not the mean
options.why: Both are computed on future days.
The folds came after the leak; the scaled values already carry the future.

feedback.correct: A full-sample scaler leaks the future into every fold; fit it on each training fold.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Which data did the scaler see?

explain.text: `validation` level 3's rule: preprocessing is part of the model, so fit it inside each fold.
